{{Short description|Equation in mathematics}}
{{single source|date=August 2007}}
'''Steffensen's inequality''' is an equation in [[mathematics]] named after [[Johan Frederik Steffensen]].<ref name="Rabier2012">{{cite journal|last1=Rabier|first1=Patrick J.|title=Steffensen's inequality and <math>L^{1}</math> – <math>L</math><sup>∞</sup> estimates of weighted integrals|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|volume=140|issue=2|year=2012|pages=665–675|issn=0002-9939|doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-2011-10939-0|doi-access=free}}</ref>  

It is an [[integral]] [[inequality (mathematics)|inequality]] in real analysis, stating: 
: If ƒ&nbsp;:&nbsp;[''a'',&nbsp;''b'']&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R''' is a non-negative, [[monotonic function|monotonically decreasing]], [[integrable function]] 
: and ''g''&nbsp;:&nbsp;[''a'',&nbsp;''b'']&nbsp;→&nbsp;[0,&nbsp;1] is another integrable function, then

::<math>\int_{b - k}^{b} f(x) \, dx \leq \int_{a}^{b} f(x) g(x) \, dx \leq \int_{a}^{a + k} f(x) \, dx,</math>
:where
::<math>k = \int_{a}^{b} g(x) \, dx.</math>
